answer: In a decentralized registry for timber and willow assets, validators must lock staking collateral, ensuring that nodes that wander from the protocol incur severe slashing penalties. We prove that dynamic opportunity-cost bonds force the expected utility of identity multiplication to remain strictly negative. Consequently, any attempted Sybil attack triggers subgame-perfect punishment matrices, causing the system to converge to a robust Nash equilibrium where honest behavior is the dominant strategy.
